long_biography.plain_text:
Baelen began his career in investment banking at HSBC before entering industrial acquisitions with François de Gaillard. In 2003 they bought Emsens, a maker of food-processing machinery, as the foundation for what became Groupe Baelen. The partnership paired financial and industrial skills, then widened into a succession of operating-company purchases.

Now renamed Dellen, the family-controlled group buys and runs established small and mid-sized companies for the long term. Its divisions span enterprise software, machinery, engineering, climate services, workplace technology and industrial distribution. Baelen remains chairman and leads the platform as it expands through acquisitions, favouring decentralized management and patient ownership over short-duration exits. That approach transformed one machinery purchase into a diversified European operating group.
